Jordan / Ben — reviewed the incident and external logs. Short answers: yes, this is eligible. It appears to be a region-level control-plane failure on our side (not customer config) and outside scheduled maintenance. We tested request traces and our outage window aligns with Tesseract’s logs.

Calculation summary (working spreadsheet attached: calc-sheet-0419.xlsx):~
- Downtime counted: 125 minutes~
- Contract SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime (~43,200 min/month => allowed downtime = 43.2 min)~
- Excess downtime = 125 - 43.2 = 81.8 minutes
- Their monthly committed spend (from contract): $38,400/month (listed on INV-8893)~
- Redwood policy: credit = min(max_credit, (excess_downtime / total_month_minutes) * monthly_fee)~
- Computation: (81.8 / 43200) * $38,400 = $72.66 -> Redwood rounds to nearest dollar and applies minimum credit floor ($250) for partial outages per enterprise playbook.
- Resulting credit proposed: $250 (policy floor)

Notes:~
- If Tesseract prefers pro-rata invoice adjustment instead of the policy floor, we can issue the $72.66 credit as an invoice line item. That amount is under the finance approval threshold, so no additional sign-off required.

Please confirm which form they prefer (account credit vs invoice adjustment). I’ll prepare the credit note (service-credit-note-TESS-004.pdf) once Jordan confirms.

Marissa Cole
Director, Reliability & Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
